'''Paula Ruth Williamson''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FMedSci}} is a British medical statistician who specialises in medical statistics and the use of methodology within the field, particularly clinical trials methodology. A graduate from the [[University of Sheffield]], she originally worked as a senior statistician in healthcare before moving to the [[University of Liverpool]], where she became Professor of Medical Statistics and served as head of the Department of Biostatistics from 2002 until 2018. She was elected [[Fellow of the Academy of Medical Sciences]] in 2018.

==Biography==
Paula Ruth Williamson<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Paula Ruth Williamson |url=https://acmedsci.ac.uk/fellows/fellows-directory/ordinary-fellows/fellow/Paula%20Ruth-Williamson-0013267 |access-date=2024-03-29 |website=Academy of Medical Sciences}}</ref> was educated at the [[University of Sheffield]], where she got her Bachelor of Science degree with special honours in Probability and Statistics and eventually her [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in Probability and Statistics.<ref name="academia-net"/> Her doctoral dissertation was titled ''Prognostic prediction within Cox's proportional hazards regression model''.<ref name="academia-net">{{Cite web |title=Prof. Paula Williamson |url=https://www.academia-net.org/profile/paula-williamson/78375 |access-date=2024-03-29 |website=Academia-Net}}</ref>

She worked abroad as a senior research assistant at the [[Kirby Institute|National Centre in HIV Epidemiology and Clinical Research]] in Australia from 1990 until 1991, and having worked as a statistical tutor while studying for her PhD in Sheffield, later continued her tutor work abroad at the [[University of Sydney]]'s Department of Mathematical Statistics in 1990.<ref name="academia-net" /> She worked as a senior statistician at the Yorkshire Clinical Trials and Research Unit (1992-1994) and the Central Manchester Healthcare Trust Department of [[Medical genetics|Medical Genetics]] (1994-1996).<ref name="academia-net" /> She also worked as a geographer, during which she had some experience in statistics; she recalled this during a November 1999 meeting organised by the [[Royal Statistical Society]]'s Merseyside Local Group.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2000 |title=Report of the Council for the Session 1999-2000 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2681036 |journal=Journal of the Royal Statistical Society. Series D (The Statistician) |volume=49 |issue=4 |pages=582 |jstor=2681036 |issn=0039-0526 }}</ref>

In 1996, Williamson moved to the [[University of Liverpool]] Department of Mathematical Sciences and started as a lecturer, before being promoted to senior lecturer in 2000 and reader at the Centre for Medical Statistics and Health Evaluation in 2002.<ref name="academia-net" /> In 2005, she was promoted to professor at the Department of Biostatistics,<ref name="academia-net" /> where she served as head from 2002 to 2018.<ref name="hdruk" /> She later moved to the University's Institute of [[Population health|Population Health]] and became Professor of Medical Statistics.<ref name="liverpool">{{Cite web |title=Paula Williamson |url=https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/population-health/staff/paula-williamson/ |access-date=2024-03-29 |website=University of Liverpool Institute of Population Health}}</ref> She has also held several positions in government institutions, including chair of the [[Medical Research Council (United Kingdom)|Medical Research Council]]'s Network of Hubs for Trials Methodology Research (2008-2018) and [[National Institute for Health and Care Research]] Senior Investigator.<ref name="hdruk">{{Cite web |title=Paula Williamson |url=https://www.hdruk.ac.uk/people/paula-williamson/ |access-date=2024-03-29 |website=Health Data Research UK |language=en-GB}}</ref> In 2021, she was elected to the Council of the [[Academy of Medical Sciences]].<ref name="liverpool" />

As an academic, Williamson specialises in medical statistics and the use of methodology within the field, particularly clinical trials methodology.<ref name="acmedsci" /><ref name="Bradford Hall" /> In 2017, she was the speaker for the 26th [[Bradford Hill Memorial Lecture]], "Improving health by improving trials: from outcomes to recruitment and back again".<ref name="Bradford Hall">{{Cite web |title=26th Bradford Hill Memorial Lecture |url=https://www.lshtm.ac.uk/newsevents/events/26th-bradford-hill-memorial-lecture |access-date=2024-03-29 |website=London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine |language=en}}</ref> She was elected [[Fellow of the Academy of Medical Sciences]] in 2018.<ref name="acmedsci">{{Cite web |title=Professor Paula Williamson |url=https://acmedsci.ac.uk/fellows/fellows-directory/ordinary-fellows/fellow/Professor-Paula-Williamson-0020710 |access-date=2024-03-29 |website=Academy of Medical Sciences}}</ref>
